**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/25 (Thu) 16:21  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The /show command allows you to move a job to another server or channel, revive a lost job, or refresh an old job to make new variations, upscale, or use newer parameters and features.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The command requires a Job ID, which is a unique identifier for each image generated by Midjourney.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Job IDs can be found in the first part of all image filenames, in the URLs on the website, and in an image's filename.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To use the /show command, type '/show <Job ID>' in any Bot Channel to revive a Job.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The /show command only works for your own jobs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To find a Job ID:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] On the Web: Select ... > Copy... > Job ID in the member gallery.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] From the URL: The last part of the URL when viewing an image in the member gallery.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] From the File Name: The last part of the file name when viewing an image downloaded from the member gallery.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Animated Gif Showing how to use the Midjourney Show command is also provided.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The /blend command allows you to upload 2–5 images quickly and then looks at the concepts and aesthetics of each image and merges them into a novel new image.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] /blend is the same as using multiple image prompts with /imagine, but the interface is optimized for easy use on mobile devices.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] /blend works with up to 5 images.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To use more than 5 images in a prompt, use image prompts with /imagine.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] /blend does not work with text prompts.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To use text and image prompts together, use image prompts and text with /imagine.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] After typing the /blend command, you will be prompted to upload two photos.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] You can drag and drop images from your hard drive or add images from your photo library when using a mobile device.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To add more images, select the optional/options field and select image3, image4, or image5.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The /blend command may take longer to start than other commands
